hrp,005056a3-d347-1fe1-99ba-5ec05c8842a8,16935235,"Manager, Curriculum Development (Social Science)",Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura,0000009048,"The Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (Muis), also known as the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore, was established as a statutory body in 1968 when the Administration of Muslim Law Act (AMLA) came into effect. Muis is a statutory board under the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY). It seeks to develop a Muslim community with strong Islamic credentials that thrives in the contemporary world, and is an active partner in nation-building. At Muis, we strive to fulfil the values of compassion and inclusiveness. The Senior Curriculum Developer/Faculty Member will contribute to the development and delivery of an innovative undergraduate degree programme curriculum for the Singapore College of Islamic Studies (SCIS), combining advanced interdisciplinary Islamic scholarship with cutting-edge pedagogical methods to create learner-centred, industry-relevant curricula for multicultural Singapore.


The successful candidate will bridge modern Social Science disciplines with traditional Islamic knowledge andwith modern interdisciplinary approaches, preparing future Asatizah who are adept in applying Islamic principles and social science concepts and theories to navigate contemporary societal challenges. As a potential future faculty member of SCIS, this role offers the opportunity to contribute to institutional academic development whilst advancing interdisciplinary Islamic studies through research, quality teaching, and curriculum innovation.

Applicants will be appointed as either Senior Curriculum Developer only or Senior Curriculum Developer/Faculty Member based on appropriate qualifications, expertise and experience.

","

The SCIS undergraduate degree programme’s curriculum structure includes modules that will be offered by partner universities and those that will be developed in-house.

The Senior Curriculum Developer/Faculty Member will be tasked to develop the in-house undergraduate module packages which will include the syllabi, assessment plan, instructional materials, recommended readings, digital learning resources, textbooks, etc.​ They will also be tasked to deliver these modules, if appropriate.

They will each be assigned to minimally one of these 3 focus areas.
a) Thematic Modules

b) Social Science/ Social Development Modules

c) Interdisciplinary Tutorials

Core Competencies:

1. Curriculum Design Expertise (including Pedagogy & Assessment) & Delivery Excellence: Develop and enhance learner-centred, industry-relevant curriculum that engages learners, using effective teaching methods, educational technology, and assessment approaches for higher education whilst maintaining ethical integrity and fostering an inclusive learning environment. Experience in teaching in blended or online modes using learner centred methods, particularly applied learning methods at higher education level will be advantageous.

2. Scholarly Expertise and Research Excellence: Deep knowledge of the foundational social science disciplines such as Sociology, Political Science, Economics, Area Studies, Religious Studies, and/or humanities (eg. History and Philosophy) and disciplines within the domain of social development (such as Counselling, Social Work, Psychology etc) combined with competence in conducting academic research, critical analysis, and contributing to knowledge creation within Islamic studies and related fields. Research interest in topics such as social cohesion, family, religion in plural societies, politics and governance, history, intersections of science, technology and religion, gender studies and the study of Muslim communities will be an advantage.

3. Interdisciplinary Integration and Contemporary Relevance: Ability to meaningfully connect Islamic knowledge with insights from social sciences and humanities, applying interdisciplinary Islamic teachings to current societal challenges and contexts to make religious knowledge practical and meaningful for contemporary multicultural Singapore.

4. Academic Communication and Collaboration: Excellent academic writing and presentation skills - in English and/or Arabic languages - for developing course materials and programme documentation. Strong interpersonal abilities for collaborating effectively with team members, curriculum coordinators and course administrators across different subject areas.

5. Time Management: Proven ability to manage curriculum design timelines effectively, balancing thorough academic development with institutional deadlines. Skills in prioritising tasks across different aspects of the curriculum and ensuring timely delivery of course materials and programme documentation.

Additional Competencies:

1. Technology Integration: Proficiency in educational technology platforms suitable for interdisciplinary higher education including digital libraries, online learning and multimedia resources is advantageous.

","

Qualifications:

Tertiary education in Social Sciences, Humanities, Islamic Studies, Islamic Law, Educational Philosophy, or related interdisciplinary fields, with a strong foundation in humanities and social sciences scholarship from recognised institutions. International academic credentials, particularly from established universities, are highly valued.

There are two vacancies available for this post.

The Community Chest, formed since 1983, is the largest centralised fund-raising body for social services in Singapore to lighten social service organisations from the burden of fund-raising. The mandate of the Group was expanded in 2015 to include the role of Secretariat to the President’s Challenge, Office of the President of Singapore, and has gone beyond traditional fund-raising to engaging the community, public, family offices, foundations and the corporates in creating sustainable solutions to address social challenges and foster a more inclusive society.

The role as we see it.

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced individual to join our Philanthropic Partnerships team, focusing on fundraising and partnership development with donors from Public Agencies, and Community Groups (such as Clans, Education, Healthcare and Religious Institutions).

In this role, you will be responsible for crafting and executing strategies to engage philanthropic donors, corporations, and partners to support the mission and programs of the Community Chest of Singapore. You will lead efforts to secure funding while building long-term partnerships that maximize resources and drive social impact.

You should take pride in your commitment to excellence, both individually and within a team, possess a keen attention to detail and thrive in a fast-paced, high-performance environment. We place a premium on your ability in managing demanding stakeholder relationships with professionalism and poise. You excel under pressure, adeptly resolve conflicts, and focus on building sustainable, long-term partnerships.

","

Areas you should be passionate about and excel in.

1. Strategy Development: Create and implement comprehensive strategies to engage philanthropic donors and partners, aligning efforts with the organization's mission and objectives. Identify and establish partnerships with philanthropic donors, corporations, government agencies, trade associations, and Social Service Agencies (SSAs) to leverage resources and maximize impact. Identify and cultivate new donor segments/revenue streams by leveraging the extensive suite of NCSS resources, including matching grants and government-backed initiatives.

2. Sector Development & Advocacy: Foster and maintain strong relationships with individual donors, foundations, corporations, and other stakeholders to increase the giving of Time, Treasure and Talent. Lead sector-specific fundraising initiatives, including campaigns, events, and appeals, in close coordination with internal and external stakeholders.

3. Collaboration & Stakeholder Management: Collaborate closely with internal teams to ensure fundraising efforts are aligned with organizational goals. Work with Committees and key stakeholders to strategise and implement various philanthropic and volunteerism initiatives.

4. Donor Management, Insights and Reporting: Develop and maintain systems for tracking and reporting on fundraising activities to ensure accountability and transparency. Utilize and refine donor data and insights to enhance donor experience and satisfaction. Ensure risk management / mitigation on systems and public facing platforms and touchpoints.

5. Strategic Communication: Craft compelling messages and materials that effectively convey the impact of philanthropic support and partnerships to donors, partners, and the broader community.

The incumbent will manage a portfolio of current and prospective donors and oversee all phases of the gift cycle including donor engagement, cultivation, solicitation, proposal development, and stewardship. This role will also support the College’s leadership team in designing and implementing strategies to secure significant philanthropic gifts, while working closely with volunteers, senior leadership, faculty, and colleagues to advance the College’s priorities.

Climate change poses an asymmetrical challenge for Singapore – we contribute only around 0.1% of global carbon emissions, but will be disproportionately impacted by its effects.

In Feb 2021, the Government launched the Singapore Green Plan 2030, a whole-of-nation movement to advance Singapore’s national agenda on sustainable development. In Oct 2022, Singapore announced that it would raise its national climate target to achieve net zero emissions by 2050.

There is much work to be done to realise the climate aspirations of Singapore. The available mitigation options have trade-offs, and need to be considered in the context of the overall triple transition of carbon, energy and the economy. Your work will therefore revolve around carefully weighing trade-offs, whether that be in exploring new possibilities for Singapore or ensuring existing policies remain fit-for-purpose.","Climate action is a priority for MSE, and is driven by the Energy & Climate Policy Division (ECPD). ECPD drives policies relating to climate science, climate adaptation and climate mitigation, including issues such as carbon pricing, decarbonising Singapore’s economy, coastal protection, and reducing urban heat. The key scope of work for the position is to provide operational support of Energy Management Systems which involves round the clock monitoring and control of electricity generators as well as the electricity and natural gas transmission networks. In addition, the position is also required to operate a Cybersecurity Operation Centre to monitor cybersecurity threats and manage Power Sector Critical Information Infrastructure incidents.

","

Job Description

Energy Management System

• Provide first-level technical support to the Energy Management System to ensure high availability and reliability. This includes attending to technical problem reported by Power System Operators, operations and maintenance of Energy Management System, other supporting operational technology systems, OT/IT network & security infrastructures to ensure these systems (both hardware and software applications) are of high availability and reliability.

• Participates in the design and technical enhancements on mission-critical Energy Management Systems (EMS) such as integrating renewables such as solar, energy storage and electricity imports into EMS to meet operational business requirements. This also includes fine tuning of power system applications to support real-time operations such as power system studies (e.g. Contingency Analysis, Transmission Network Analysis, Short Circuit Analysis), Automatic Generation Control, load forecast, solar PV forecast, telemetry, State Estimator, and the Dispatcher Training Simulator.

• Coordinate with Licenseses’ to facilitate connection of new generation facilities, transmission network equipment (both electricity and gas systems) including performing updates and validate of EMS databases with field equipment and market operation.

Cyber Security Monitoring for Power Sector

• Provide first-level technical support for Cyber Security Operation Centre (CSOC) to manage cyber incident that may cause severe impact to Power System Operation and Power Sector's Critical Information Infrastructures (CIIs). Job responsibilities include analysing security alerts, identifying anomalies, report findings to stakeholders. Perform daily triage of the security cases and following up with CII Operators and resolution of incidents reported.

Cybersecurity Risk Assessment & Management

• Develops and implement technical solutions, including cyber security mitigation measures and/or configuration changes to enhance the security posture of the Energy Management Systems and meet regulatory requirements such as Cybersecurity Act and CCoP.

• Coordinate security reviews risk assessments, security audits that can effectively pre-empt and identify significant security gaps or weaknesses. This include carrying out periodic documentation reviews, testing and implementing recommendations by the auditors, and performing system patching.

• In addition, the department also maintain other critical supporting infrastructure such as Uninterruptible Power Supply, fire protection system, security access system etc to ensure reliable operation of the EMS system and the operation centres.

","

What the role is

You will be part of the team that develops the specialised engineering capabilities required to establish EMA as an informed technical lead on advanced nuclear power systems. You will be responsible for building internal capabilities to evaluate the engineering feasibility and safety profiles of complex energy technologies, ensuring that the organization can benchmark global designs against international safety, security, and safeguards standards.

","

What you will be working on:

1. Engineering Benchmarking & Technical Modelling

  • Technical Specialisation: Build specialised institutional expertise in advanced thermal-hydraulic systems, core physics, and material behaviour for next-generation nuclear energy technologies.

  • Multi-disciplinary Assessment: Conduct engineering research across Civil, Mechanical, and Electrical disciplines to verify the technical claims of emerging global technologies.

  • Conceptual Modelling: Support the development of technical benchmarks and reference architectures for various advanced reactor concepts (e.g., Light Water SMRs and High-Temperature Gas-cooled Reactors).

  • Feasibility Research: Study how global engineering designs might theoretically be optimised, exploring concepts like modular construction and system co-location.

  • Hazard Modelling: Develop capabilities in high-level hazard identification and risk modelling using methodologies such as Probabilistic Risk Assessment (PRA) and Fault Tree Analysis to understand theoretical failure modes.

  • Safety Case Research: Study the development of safety cases to understand how deterministic and probabilistic engineering controls align.

  • Technical Standards Governance: Build frameworks to evaluate how design modifications might affect the overall integrity of a technology's safety envelope.

3. Strategic Technical Partnerships

  • Technical Collaboration: Coordinate with international engineering consultants and research organizations to facilitate knowledge transfer and capability building.

  • Standards Advocacy: Act as a technical lead in researching how international engineering standards can be applied to optimise advanced technology for compact land-use constraints.

  • Technology Horizon Scanning: Monitor global trends in advanced nuclear technology (e.g., SMRs and Generation IV systems) to provide data-driven technical insights to senior leadership.

As the Head of the Planning & Governance Branch, you will serve as the department’s central lead for organizational framework development and international compliance research. You will lead the establishment of Integrated Management Systems (IMS) and governance structures necessary to support long-term feasibility studies.
You will translate complex, multi-branch activities into an integrated programme view, enabling senior leadership and policymakers to understand progress, risks, trade-offs, and readiness at different milestones.

","

What you will be working on

1. Leadership & Management Scope

  • Framework Design: Lead the design and implementation of an Integrated Management System (IMS) based on international benchmarks (e.g., IAEA GSR Part 2), ensuring that quality, safety, and economic elements are synthesized into a single organizational framework.

  • Operational Excellence: Establish internal decision-making protocols and quality assurance processes essential for managing high-complexity technical projects.

  • Capability Building: Lead the professional development of the branch, ensuring the team is equipped with the specialized expertise required to navigate international regulatory landscapes and complex project governance.

2. Financial Governance & Commercial Readiness

  • Economic Modeling: Direct the analysis of financial governance frameworks and long-term funding models for complex infrastructure, including cost-benefit studies and lifecycle economic assessments.

  • Commercial Strategy Research: Lead the study of international contracting models and procurement strategies to understand risk-sharing and vendor accountability in high-tech industries.

  • Budgetary Oversight: Manage branch-level resources and fiscal discipline to ensure transparent and efficient program management.

3. Regulatory Readiness & Licensing Roadmap

  • Readiness Roadmaps: Lead the development of comprehensive roadmaps to identify the legislative and institutional requirements for aligning with international nuclear energy benchmarks.

  • Gap Analysis: Coordinate research into global regulatory frameworks to identify potential enhancements required for local institutional readiness.

  • International Compliance: Maintain institutional expertise on international laws, treaties, and safeguards requirements, ensuring the organization remains an informed participant in global nuclear governance forums.

4. Programme Controls & Scheduling

  • Programme Governance Structures: Direct the development and maintenance of programme governance structures, including stage gates, baselines, change control, reporting, and escalation mechanisms.

  • Strategic Reporting: Provide consolidated reporting on research progress, technical risks, and resource requirements to support senior leadership in long-term strategic planning.

  • Risk Management: Oversee the high-level risk register, focusing on systemic dependencies that may impact national readiness or future policy decisions.

","

  • Quality, Environment, Health, and Safety (QEHS) System Management and Design for Safety (DfS) experience would be an advantage

  • Deep familiarity with IAEA Milestones, ISO 9001/14001/45001, or GSR Part 2 management standards.

  • Strong system integration and programme governance capability, with the ability to manage complexity across organisational boundaries.

hrp,005056a3-53e2-1fd1-98fc-22392e5df3fb,17616874,"Manager/Senior Manager (Ageing Planning Office, Centre based Care and Social Sup",Ministry of Health,0000001200,"The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. As an open country constantly exposed to an interconnected world, Singapore faces complex issues in public healthcare. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.",1779667200000,1782086400000,Closing on 22 Jun 2026,4  day(s) ago,Contract,0002,02-05 year(s),2,5,Healthcare,0014,Healthcare,0020,Healthcare,00,false,,"By 2030, almost a million Singaporeans will be aged 65 and above, and there will be an increased demand for aged care services including Senior Care Centres (SCCs) and Active Ageing Centres (AACs). To reduce social isolation and delay cognitive and physical frailty among seniors, MOH has: (i) expanded the number of AACs to support well seniors with improved the range of services and programs offered at the AACs, and (ii)  improved the capacity and utilisation of SCC services to serve a subsegment of seniors who need supervision and assistance in activities of daily living (ADL) when their caregivers are at work.

However, ground implementation of AACs and SCCs may be varied. Some AACs have managed to attract many seniors to their centres and created a lively environment for seniors, while other AACs may not be as successful in outreaching to seniors. Different SCCs may have varying services which may not fully address the emerging needs of seniors (e.g. dementia care, custodial care, community rehabilitation).

The Centre-Based Care & Social Support (CCSS) team (under the Ageing Planning Office in the Ministry of Health) is at the forefront of overseeing the overall strategy, policy, resourcing and governance for AAC and SCC services. The end goal is to enable seniors to remain well and socially engaged in the community and ensure service providers are uplifted to play such roles to support our seniors.","You will play a role in designing and implementing policies for AAC / SCC.  This includes working with MOH departments and partners such as the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) to design policy levers (e.g., care models, sector structure, and capacity planning) to meet seniors/caregiver needs in the community. You will also review resourcing models (e.g. budget, manpower, infrastructure and site allocation), develop and implement governance structures supporting the provision of AAC and SCC services, and evaluate cost-effectiveness of new service models and make recommendations. Working closely with AIC as the lead implementation partner, you will co-develop strategies that translate policy intent into outcomes on the ground.

This will also require a strong ability to collaborate closely with and work through stakeholders to implement these strategies. Public sector experience in service design, managing budgetary/procurement processes or large-scale infrastructural projects will be beneficial.

You will be working in a fast paced and highly volatile environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time. You can expect meaningful work that will improve the lived experience of seniors, while growing professionally through developing your strategy, planning and stakeholder engagement skills.","•

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. [What the role is]

STB takes a data-driven approach in tourism planning and marketing, and at the heart of it is Stan (Singapore Tourism Analytics Network, Stan), a tourism data analytics platform that allows both internal STB users and external tourism industry stakeholders to access tourism data and derive actionable insights about Singapore's tourism landscape and visitors.

As Data and AI Product Manager, you will play a pivotal role in building the data product roadmap for STB and its industry stakeholders to drive tourism growth. You'll be at the forefront of leveraging data and AI to transform Singapore's tourism industry, not just defining what needs to be built, but getting hands-on to prove it works before it scales. Success in this position means delivering data and AI-enabled products that measurably enhance tourism decision-making capabilities, with demonstrated user adoption, stakeholder satisfaction, and measurable business impact on Singapore's tourism sector.

This role sits within the newly established Data Exploration and Partnerships department, reporting directly to the Head of Department, and works closely with line units across Singapore Tourism Board, government agencies, and industry partners to drive data-driven decision-making and insights generation in tourism.

","

[What you will be working on]

As a Data and AI Product Manager, your key responsibilities include:

1. Data Products Roadmap Development, Planning and Execution:

a) Develop and execute the data product roadmap, defining data products required by STB and industry stakeholders, and aligned with STB's organisational goals.

b) Create and maintain comprehensive data products requirement specifications, acceptance criteria and test cases.

c) Develop mock and/or POC dashboards and datasets, to support requirements specifications and acceptance criteria.

d) Work with Stan product team to plan and implement the data products onto Stan.

e) Support testing and production verification as part of productisation process.

f) Lead product launches and go-to-market plans for major releases of data products.

g) Drive innovation in data products, constantly seeking ways to enhance value for stakeholders.

h) Proactively identify opportunities for new data products or features based on industry trends and stakeholder needs.

2. AI Roadmap, Use Cases and Proof-of-Concept Development

a) Ideate and develop the AI roadmap for STB's data platforms, identifying high-value AI use cases that enhance data accessibility and user productivity for internal and industry stakeholders.

b) Prioritise AI roadmap items using sound evaluation frameworks that weigh feasibility, impact, and implementation readiness.

c) Lead hands-on development of AI proof-of-concepts, starting with natural language query (NLQ) for conversational access to STB's datasets and analytics.

d) Design evaluation frameworks, guardrails, and test cases for AI features, ensuring reliability, accuracy, and appropriateness before productisation.

e) Identify and shape AI use cases in close collaboration with line units, translating domain needs into technically grounded AI applications.

f) Work closely with the product implementation team to ensure AI PoCs are documented and specified to a standard that enables direct handover for productisation.

g) Stay current on applied AI developments relevant to data platforms, analytics, and public sector use cases.

3. Requirements Gathering and Product Design:

a) Conduct deep dives into business scenarios, use cases, user journey mapping as part of data and AI product solution design.

b) Translate complex stakeholder needs into clear, actionable product requirements and specifications.

c) Collaborate with Data Partnerships and Stan product team to ensure product feasibility and technical alignment.

d) As part of data and AI product design and specifications, review the end-to-end processes involved in implementing and maintaining the data products, ensure processes are streamlined and efficient.

e) Leverage digital and automation tools where possible as part of the end-to-end process design i.e. WOG tools like FormSG and Plumber to automate data collection and simple data validation checks.

4. Data Governance and Quality Management for Industry-facing data domains:

a) Ensure adherence to data governance policies for data integrity, security, and compliance.

b) Support data quality management processes, ensuring the accuracy and reliability of data products as part of productisation process.

c) Apply appropriate guardrails and evaluation criteria to AI features to ensure outputs meet governance and quality standards.

5. Stakeholder Management and Communication:

a) Build and maintain strong relationships with stakeholders across STB line units, government agencies, and industry partners, with varying levels of data and tech maturity.

b)Translate complex data and AI concepts into clear, structured communications for non-technical stakeholders, facilitating understanding and buy-in.

c) Drive alignment and clarity across stakeholders, ensuring well-defined problem statements, expectations, and outcomes.

d) Collaborate cross-functionally to ensure alignment between product development, business needs, and technical capabilities.

e) Facilitate structured discussions and decision-making, especially in ambiguous or exploratory problem spaces.

6. Analytics, Experimentation and Continuous Improvement:

a) Support data pilots in identifying and solving complex data-related problems, applying critical thinking and analytical skills.

b) Support data pilots in advanced analytics, data integration and data wrangling needs.

c) Define and track key performance indicators (KPIs) for data products implemented.

d) Analyze usage pattern, stakeholder feedback and performance metrics to inform continuous improvement.

","

[What we are looking for]

The ideal candidate is formally trained in Business, Data Science, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, with at least 3–5 years of experience in data product management, data engineering, or related roles with a proven track record of delivering data-driven solutions.

Essential Skills and Knowledge

-Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down ambiguous problems into clear, actionable components, and navigate uncertainty with confidence.

-Experience evaluating pilot projects and experimental initiatives for scalability and productisation potential.

-Familiarity with data governance frameworks, data quality management, and regulatory compliance requirements.

Technical Skills

-Strong data analytics capabilities, including data exploration, transformation, and dashboard development, with proficiency in tools such as AWS QuickSight.

-Proficient in SQL and at least one programming language (Python or R).

-Hands-on experience developing or prototyping AI use cases, including prompt design, evaluation of AI outputs, and simple workflows.

-Ability to design evaluation frameworks for AI outputs, including defining metrics, test cases, and guardrails.

-Familiar with data structures and modelling required to support AI-driven use cases.

Product Management

-Proven product management skills spanning roadmap development, requirements gathering, UX design, and go-to-market execution.

-Demonstrated ability to drive products from concept to pilot to production, translating learnings into structured outcomes.

-Comfortable balancing strategic thinking with hands-on execution in early-stage product environments.

Professional Attributes

-Structured and rigorous, bringing clear frameworks and logic to complex or ambiguous problems.

-Proactive in identifying gaps and opportunities, with strong stakeholder communication and alignment skills.

-Able to work independently in evolving environments while owning workstreams end to end.

-Collaborative, hands-on, and disciplined — balancing exploration with follow-through and a strong focus on end-user value.

Additional Qualifications

Experience in tourism, hospitality, or the public sector is advantageous. Familiarity with AWS QuickSight or similar cloud analytics platforms, data integration processes, API management, and AI application development (including prompt engineering or LLM evaluation) would be a plus. Relevant certifications in product management, data engineering, or AI/ML are welcome.

",Others,Full-time

hrp,005056a3-d347-1fe1-93c8-0643d66082a2,17565357,Manager/Senior Manager (Singapore Maritime Crisis Centre,Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore,0000009045,"""The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) was established on 2 February 1996, with the mission to develop Singapore as a premier global hub port and international maritime centre (IMC), and to advance and safeguard Singapore's strategic maritime interests.
MPA is the driving force behind Singapore's port and maritime development, taking on the roles of Port Authority, Port Regulator, Port Planner, IMC Champion, and National Maritime Representative.

MPA partners the industry and other agencies to enhance safety, security and environmental protection in our port waters, facilitate port operations and growth, expand the cluster of maritime ancillary services, and promote maritime R&D and manpower development.""",1778630400000,1798588800000,Closing on 30 Dec 2026,1 month(s) ago,Fixed Terms,0006,05-15 year(s),5,15,Emergency Preparedness & Response,0025,Emergency Preparedness & Response,0015,Others,00,false,,"

The officer plays a key role towards the Whole-of-Government approach to detect and deter maritime security (MARSEC) threats in the Port of Singapore and Singapore Territorial Water (STW). This is particularly important as Singapore is strategically located at the convergence of key shipping routes around the world, with up to 70% of the world’s global maritime economy transiting through the Singapore Straits. Maritime Security is important to safeguard Singapore’s strategic maritime interest and maintains Singapore’s status as the premier hub port as well as the international maritime centre.

","

As a MPA representative, the officer will be seconded to Singapore Maritime Crisis Centre (SMCC) full time and serve as a subject matter expert for shipping industry developments, commercial shipping practices, and national and international regulations governing the shipping industry. Working closely with stakeholders, the officer is required to provide insights on maritime security and regulatory matters to support sharper sense-making to plan for a successful maritime operation. The officer will also be the key liaison between MPA departments and the seconded agency to ensure cross-agency initiatives are well communicated and executed. The officer will be required to support the conduct of exercises and workshops as well as training sessions/ visits/ seminars to enhance the Maritime organisation’s awareness and knowledge of the shipping industry.

Other operational duties can also include :

• Representing MPA on maritime security issues with other government agencies at various committees, working groups, and taking turns to perform secretariat function for these working groups etc

• Part of the planning and execution team for the Whole-of-Government (WoG) maritime security operations for key coastal events, where the officer is required to be the MPA Liaison Officer and perform duties during these Maritime operations to ensure the security of major national events, which may fall on weekends and public holidays.

• Performing Duty Officer duties (12hrs duty both day and night shift at the Command Centre) on an average of 4 times per month to manage incidents and ensure smooth operations

","

• Strong analytical, writing, communication and interpersonal skills, as well as able to work efficiently in teams

• Highly driven, organized, and able to manage multiple priorities

• Good knowledge of the shipping/ marine industry, with prior experience in this industry would be an advantage

• Candidate with working experience in related security functions in the military or national security agencies as well as good understanding of the National Maritime Security System framework will have an advantage.

• Candidate's job title at Singapore Maritime Crisis Centre (SMCC) will be in accordance with SMCC's job title framework.

• Upon the completion of the 2-year contract, suitable candidate may have the opportunity to work in other Divisions within MPA or may have their contract extended further.

",Others,Full-time

MANAGER, GIS SOLUTION & ADOPTION

","

We are looking for an experienced GIS professional to lead the standardisation and adoption of GIS solutions across LTA's engineering functions. In this role, you will work closely with engineering teams to understand their workflows, identify opportunities where GIS can add value, and develop reusable solutions that can be scaled across the organisation. You will also play a key outreach and enablement role — helping teams discover, adopt, and get the most out of GIS capabilities.

Your key responsibilities include:

  • Developing a thorough understanding of engineering workflows and processes across the organisation, building a clear picture of functional needs and priority pain points.
  • Defining and maintaining a structured framework of GIS use cases organised by common workflows, user groups, and data needs — mapping existing solutions against this framework to identify gaps, duplication, and opportunities for standardisation.
  • Designing and maintaining reusable GIS templates and solution frameworks, including for areas not yet served by existing tools, and assessing enterprise systems and platforms to ensure GIS solutions are fit for purpose.
  • Creating clear, task-based user guides and quick-start materials to help non-expert users get up and running with reusable templates.
  • Planning and leading outreach initiatives across Groups to showcase GIS capabilities, gather feedback, and drive uptake — including facilitating workshops and clinics to support users, address technical queries, and foster knowledge sharing.
  • Continuously scanning for opportunities to broaden the application of GIS across the organisation, translating these into proposed pilots, standards, or roadmap items.

","

  • At least 10 years of experience in GIS, geospatial solutions, or related fields, with a demonstrated track record of delivering solutions for engineering, infrastructure, utilities, or asset management contexts.
  • Strong ability to elicit requirements from users, understand end-to-end workflows, and translate them into practical, scalable solutions — from prototype through to full rollout.
  • Hands-on experience creating reusable GIS assets such as templates, data models, map and app patterns, symbology standards, and reference architectures.
  • Working knowledge of enterprise applications and data platforms — such as EAM/CMMS, document management systems, BIM/CAD tools, and data lakes — and how GIS integrates with them.
  • Ability to produce clear, accessible documentation for diverse audiences including engineers, planners, and operational teams.
  • Experience designing and delivering workshops, training, or enablement programmes to drive adoption and build user capability.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills, with the ability to facilitate alignment and influence outcomes across teams without relying on formal authority.
  • A proactive and strategic mindset — with the ability to spot opportunities, prioritise value, and drive continuous improvement through well-designed standards and reusable solutions.

As part of the shortlisting process for the role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and /or undergo further assessment.

",Others,Full-time

hrp,005056a3-53e2-1fd1-97cb-b5a2f13bd3fa,17565129,"(Senior) Assistant Director/Manager, Integrated Operations (Procurement)",Ministry of National Development,0000001140,"The Ministry of National Development (MND), the lead government agency responsible for land use planning and infrastructure development, aims to transform Singapore into an endearing home and a distinctive global city. About EDB
column2:
The Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB), a government agency under the Ministry of Trade and Industry, is responsible for strategies that enhance Singapore’s position as a global centre for business, innovation, and talent. We undertake investment promotion and industry development, and work with international businesses, both foreign and local, by providing information, connection to partners and access to government incentives for their investments. Our mission is to create sustainable economic growth, with vibrant business and good job opportunities for Singapore.

For more information on EDB, please visit www.edb.gov.sg

About SGN
The Singapore Global Network (SGN) is a division under EDB and focuses on building a strong ecosystem of overseas family, friends and fans of Singapore. This includes growing a network of individuals whose skills, affinity and influence could strengthen Singapore’s business and talent ecosystem, along with enhancing international mindshare of Singapore as a vibrant global hub in Asia.

The Communities & Networks team is responsible for driving region specific efforts to grow and engage SGN’s global networks. The global team comprises officers who develop and execute strategies either from the Singapore office or one of SGN’s overseas offices. For more information on SGN, please visit www.singaporeglobalnetwork.gov.sg

","

We’re looking for a Market Director in Americas to grow and activate SGN’s network across the region. In this role, you will work closely with colleagues in EDB and across government, as well as in-market partners ranging from industry to community organisations to develop and execute market development strategies for our activities.

This role includes a probationary period to assess performance and suitability, after which the role will be based in the Americas.

Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Planning and executing digital and in-person strategies to grow, engage, and foster community within SGN’s network of members in Americas. This includes designing and delivering both one-to-one and one-to-many engagements.

  • Driving market strategy by identifying opportunities and analysing ground sentiments in the Americas, translating insights into actionable strategies that support SGN’s objectives and broader national priorities.

  • Identifying, developing and maintaining a network of corporate / community partners who can achieve SGN’s business outcomes.

  • Collaborating with other EDB divisions and Singapore Government agencies to connect global networks with economic and national priorities.

","

  • A university degree in any discipline with at least 5 years of working experience in marketing, international relations or community building. Relevant overseas working experiences will be a bonus.

  • Strong interest in current affairs and knowledge of latest developments in Singapore and trending global issues.

  • Proven ability to build, manage, and sustain relationships with diverse stakeholders.

  • Energetic, sociable, empathetic and comfortable engaging a cross-cultural audience.

  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, in both written and spoken English. Additional language skills (e.g. Mandarin, Bahasa Melayu, etc.) would be a bonus.

  • Exceptional organisational and project management skills, able to manage multiple complex projects concurrently.

  • Highly adaptable, able to work independently and in cross-functional teams.

  • Detail-oriented, with a high level of accuracy and quality in deliverables. Ability to travel overseas for work.

  • Prior professional experience working or based in the United States, with a strong understanding of the U.S. landscape, culture, and stakeholder environment would be a bonus.

The Corporate Planning (CP) team is part of STB’s Strategic & Corporate Planning division, which guides the strategic direction of Singapore’s tourism sector, identifying growth opportunities, assessing risks, and formulating strategies to advance on our Tourism 2040 roadmap. SCP also manages our engagement with the Board of Directors and our parent ministry, MTI.

The CP team plays a pivotal role in translating long-term strategy into actionable short- to medium-term plans, ensuring organisation-wide alignment and enabling the delivery of STB’s strategic priorities. You will work very closely with the Strategic Planning team which will plan for the longer term.

Key areas of responsibility include:

1. Corporate Planning: Lead the corporate planning cycle by setting direction, engaging with internal business units, and shaping short- to medium-term workplans.

2. Performance Management: Drive target setting, monitor performance, and report on progress to ensure alignment with STB’s strategic outcomes. Collaborate with senior management to define both STB’s and the broader tourism industry’s aspirations and goals.

3. Ministry Engagement: Serve as STB’s primary deskhead for MTI, supporting ministry/WOG-level initiatives and facilitating coordination between STB and the ministry.

This role is ideal for you if you are keen to gain an overview of STB’s multi-faceted role in shepherding the growth of Singapore’s tourism sector, and to further develop core competencies such as corporate planning, analytical thinking, and stakeholder management.

","

As part of the Corporate Planning team, the officer will undertake, but not limited to, the following key responsibilities:

1. Lead the workstream on STB’s performance indicators and targets. The officer needs to be data-driven and regularly analyse STB’s performance through our corporate indicators, propose leading indicators, and set benchmarks based on STB’s strategies and priorities. Additionally, the officer will work with STB’s line units to seek alignment and monitor progress, organise timely, regular reviews of performance for senior management, develop and manage our annual reporting of targets and achievements to STB Board and MTI.

2. Work with relevant teams to set up the Management Dashboard on STB’s data analytics platform. The target users of the Management Dashboard are members of STB Management and line units. The officer must work closely with the technology teams to provide user needs on the desired visualisations and user experience.

3. Serve as STB’s deskhead for MTI, working with MTI to manage key reporting platforms and updates for MTI senior management, and discussions on STB’s KPIs and priorities. This includes maintaining oversight of ministry-level / whole-of-government requests and understanding the implications on STB’s planning and processes as a statutory board within the MTI-Family, as well as collating input and data across STB for ad-hoc initiatives.

4. Organise the annual corporate planning cycle for STB senior management and business units to formulate workplans in accordance with STB’s priorities. This involves the organisation of corporate planning discussions among management. The officer also needs to develop cogent and substantive guidance materials to help business units and market offices develop strong strategies for driving tourism performance.

5. In addition, officer will support industry engagement platforms such as the Tourism Industry Conference (TIC).

[Key Relationships]

Within STB, you will be able to engage across all business teams and develop a keen understanding of the tourism landscape and its operating environment. You will also work closely with MTI and other government agencies, where you would be able to learn more about the work of other economic agencies and how their work is integrated to further Singapore's economic development.

","

The candidate will play a pivotal role in facilitating business process outsourcing (BPO) arrangements, managing change and projects, driving innovation and process improvement, and overseeing performance monitoring, budgeting, and payments. This role is crucial in aligning the division's operations with organizational goals and ensuring the seamless transition and management of outsourced services.

Key Responsibilities & Competencies:

BPO Facilitation and Stakeholder Management

  • Develop a strong understanding of the business needs of account-managed divisions to facilitate the desired outsourcing arrangement.
  • Facilitate discussions and negotiations for new outsourcing processes to address pain points and improve efficiencies.
  • Competency: Stakeholder Engagement and Negotiation

Change and Project Management

  • Evaluate potential for outsourcing new business processes and review existing outsourced work, including management of change requests for scope of service, pricing, and volume.
  • Develop and execute comprehensive transition plans from current to new vendor, ensuring minimal disruption to operations.
  • Apply project management methodologies to oversee concurrent initiatives.
  • Competency: Project Management and Change Management

Innovation and Process Improvement

  • Facilitate discussions and evaluation of innovation proposals to enhance performance of outsourced work.
  • Support process streamlining initiatives.
  • Monitor and track potential savings from implemented innovations.
  • Competency: Innovation and Process Optimization

Performance Monitoring, Budgeting and Payment

  • Monitor and prepare dashboards/reports of performance metrics.
  • Ensure alignment with contractual requirements and maintain service partner capacity at optimal levels.
  • Perform budget projections and financial transactions for payment of service fees.
  • Competency: Financial Acumen and Performance Monitoring

","

Job Requirements:

  • Possess the required competencies to execute the job duties proficiently, at least 6 years of relevant working experience (Senior Manager), at least 3 to 5 years of relevant experience (Manager).
  • Strong project management skills with experience in managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects.
  • Experience in planning and executing large-scale transitions between service providers and knowledge of government procurement processes is advantageous.
  • Confidence to engage internal and external stakeholders at different levels independently.
  • Proficiency in MS Office, especially Excel, and project management tools.
  • Analytical and meticulous, particularly when working with complex documents and specifications.

This is an individual contributor role.

Successful candidates will be offered a 2-year contract in the first instance and may be considered for an extension or be placed on a permanent tenure

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.",1780876800000,1782000000000,Closing on 21 Jun 2026,5  day(s) ago,Permanent/Contract,0003,03-05 year(s),3,5,Policy & Planning,0025,Policy & Planning,0021,Others,00,false,,"The Division:

Singapore keeps healthcare affordable through government subsidies and the 3Ms: MediShield Life, MediSave and MediFund. For these schemes to work, every part of the supporting systems must function accurately and without interruption. The Finance Systems Policy (FSP) division at MOH owns the systems that make this possible. These include the National Platform for Healthcare Claims, means-testing systems administering healthcare subsidise such as the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), and the accreditation framework that governs which institutions and practitioners may participate in financing schemes. Together, these systems process tens of thousands of claims daily and form the operational backbone of Singapore's healthcare financing architecture.
The Role:

Your starting assignment is the Financing Schemes Accreditation E-service (FSAE) system. Before a patient can use MediSave or MediShield Life at a medical institution, that institution and its practitioners must be accredited by MOH. FSAE manages that process: it handles accreditation applications, verifications, and decisions for medical institutions and practitioners across Singapore. The system operates across multiple agencies, including the Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB), the Singapore Medical Council (SMC), the Singapore Dental Council (SDC), and the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) and so on.

A practitioner who cannot submit claims means a patient who cannot access financing for their treatments. Keeping accreditation accurate, expedient, and aligned with policy is what this role exists to do.
Over time, as you develop your understanding of FSP's portfolio, there is scope to take on other systems within the division. The capabilities you build on one system transfer directly to others.
You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time","Product Ownership

You will be responsible for FSAE and its related accreditation systems end-to-end. This means understanding what each system does, why it was designed the way it was, where it falls short, and how it can be improved. You will work with MOH policy teams, IT vendors, and technical teams to translate requirements into system design, develop and prioritise the feature roadmap, conduct usability and end-to-end testing, and ensure that changes work as intended before they reach end-users.
Policy-to-System Translation

Healthcare financing schemes evolve continuously. New services become claimable. Accreditation criteria are updated. Licensing requirements change under the Healthcare Services Act. Each change requires someone who understands both the policy intent and the system's behaviour well enough to ensure nothing is lost in translation. This thread is a distinct part of the role, not a subset of product ownership.
Operational Continuity

Accreditation is not a set-and-forget process. Institutions encounter issues. Data needs to be reviewed and sometimes corrected. Systemic problems need to be identified, traced, and resolved before they compound. You will maintain oversight of day-to-day system health, manage data access and sharing in accordance with whole-of-government data governance guidelines, and handle requests from external stakeholders appropriately.
This is not a delivery coordination role. It requires genuine ownership of both the policy intent behind a system and the technical design that carries it out.
The Team:
You will report to an Assistant Director in FSP and work within a division of about 14 officers.

FSP runs a structured capability development programme for its officers, built around four areas: product thinking, policy domain knowledge, communications, and technical skills. In practical terms, this means that 18 months in, you should be able to read a policy paper and interrogate whether FSAE's design actually implements it, hold your own in a technical review with a vendor, and produce a brief that helps Senior Management make a good decision.","We are looking for someone with 3 to 5 years of working experience in policy, operations, technology, or a field that required you to translate between these domains.

Beyond that, what matters is how you think. You should be able to form a clear view from incomplete information, hold it under pressure, and communicate it without ambiguity across technical, operational, and policy teams.
Key competencies required:

column2: Thinking Clearly and Making Sound Judgements.  In FSP, this means tracing why a system behaves the way it does, identifying where it diverges from policy intent, and forming a clear recommendation with the evidence available, not the evidence you wish you had.

Learning and Putting Skills into Action.  Healthcare financing is a domain you build over time. What matters is the drive to understand it rigorously and to apply what you learn in a system where the consequences are real.

Improving and Innovating.  FSP's systems serve a policy environment that changes. The ability to identify where a process or system has not kept pace, and to propose a concrete improvement while managing the risks of change, is central to this role.

Working Effectively with Stakeholders.  FSAE operates across MOH, CPFB, AIC, SMC, and SDC and others. The ability to work across agencies, technical teams, and policy owners to reach a clear and workable outcome is not optional.

column1: Your background is less important than how you approach problems. That said, the following thinking patterns tend to predict success in this role:

column2: You ask why something works the way it does before accepting that it does.
You can hold a policy document in one hand and a system specification in the other, and identify where they diverge.
You build your position from evidence, not from what the room expects you to say.
You treat stakeholder complexity as a problem to be structured, not managed around.

Formerly known as Singapore Corporation of Rehabilitative Enterprises (SCORE), Yellow Ribbon Singapore (YRSG) is a statutory board under the Ministry of Home Affairs. Our purpose is to help inmates and ex-offenders rebuild their lives and lower the recidivism rate through skills and long term career development, with an effective Aftercare support network. As the lead agency championing Hope, Forgiveness, Acceptance and Second Chances for ex-offenders, we strive towards building a safer and more inclusive Singapore.
Beyond Second Chances

Without second chances, a released offender will leave the first physical prison and find himself entering into a second social prison. Therefore, it is not enough to give an offender a skill, we need to offer him a job that can lead to a long-term career. It is not enough to ask an offender to renounce his gang and past, his family needs to accept him back, and the community must be ready to reintegrate him. However, ex-offenders are not mere recipients of second chances. When successfully reintegrated, they can pay it forward and actively give back to the community too. As individuals, or collectively as a community. Individuals, organisations and employers do not just offer second chances when they can accept an ex-offender. In fact, their actions inspire others as well. Together, our collective effort can build a safer and more inclusive society.

At Yellow Ribbon Singapore, we aim to build a community where ex-offenders are empowered to look beyond their past and towards the future. Do you love Singapore for punching above its weight as a Little Red Dot? Can you identify with the grit exhibited by our founding leaders and generation as they worked hard to build Singapore to what it is today? Do you believe that history comes alive when it is shared across generations? If the answer is ""yes"", join us at the Founders' Memorial (FM)!

At the FM, we are creating a brand-new garden-museum experience for Singaporeans, by Singaporeans – a national landmark at the heart of our garden city that uncovers the story of how independent Singapore came to be, and brings Singaporeans across generations together to reflect and have bold conversations about what our founding values mean today and for our future.

The FM is seeking a passionate and creative individual to join the Education and Interpretation team, developing interpretive experiences that bring the story of Singapore's founding to life for families and younger visitors and promote inter-generational connection. You will play a key role in making FM's exhibitions and programmes accessible and meaningful across generations – translating rich historical content into engaging, age-appropriate experiences that spark curiosity and conversation. Look forward to being a part of creating a living Memorial that unites, challenges and inspires Singaporeans of all generations towards a brighter future!

","

  • Family interpretive layers for exhibitions: Working closely with another member in the team, you will develop the interpretive layers for families across FM's permanent and special exhibitions – translating complex historical narratives into accessible and engaging content for visitors of different ages. This includes developing family-oriented resources such as activity sheets, guides, and other interpretive materials that support inter-generational exploration and conversation within the exhibition. You will work collaboratively with the Curatorial and Exhibitions teams to ensure that the family interpretive layer is well-integrated into the overall exhibition experience. You will also be involved in the fitout of a dedicated Family Space in the Memorial which will support regular family programmes (such as storytelling and craft activities) post-opening.

  • Project Citizens: As part of the Education and Interpretation team, you will contribute to the collecting and processing of stories collected through "Project Citizens" – FM's public call for stories of the founding generation, launched in 2025. Beyond processing the stories for display, you will take an active role in following up with contributors, which include conducting further interviews and coordinating photography and video documentation, to develop richer story features for the Project Citizens wall at the Memorial. This aspect of work calls for sensitivity and care, and the ability to build rapport with seniors.

  • Content development for exhibitions for inter-generational audiences: Post-opening, you will support the development of interpretive layers and activities for families for special exhibitions and events, as well as installations and exhibitions designed specifically for inter-generational audiences at the Memorial. You will be required to draw on your understanding and research on how inter-generational audiences engage with content at museums, to ensure that FM remains a welcoming and meaningful destination for visitors of all ages.

  • Preferably at least 2–3 years of experience in a related role, preferably in a museum, heritage institution, or educational setting.

  • Demonstrated ability to conduct historical research and translate complex content into accessible, engaging points of engagement for family and inter-generational audiences.

  • Audience Management - Ability to develop and implement complex engagement strategies and activities that cater to different visitor segments, evaluate the effectiveness of engagement strategies and activities, lead and manage programming teams to develop engagement ideas and concepts that align with objectives.

What the role is

Planning and Intelligence Division (PID) is part of SWDA’s Incentives Management and Enforcement Group (IMEG). IMEG drives organisational excellence by delivering trusted, data-driven operations that strengthen governance, manage risk, and safeguard public confidence. The candidate will play a role in safeguarding the integrity of SWDA’s grant ecosystem by contributing to the formulation and review of strategies and policies aimed at countering external fraud and abuse.

","

What you will be working on

Reporting to the team lead, the successful candidate will be responsible for the following responsibilities:

Responsibilities and Competencies

Implement Data Science Projects: Collaborate with data scientists to develop, enhance, and maintain Fraud Analytics Models (FAM) aimed at effective fraud and abuse risk management. (Competency: Fraud Risk Management)

Conduct Periodic Reviews: Perform regular assessments of fraud analytics and claims analysis parameters to improve detection methods for emerging fraud and abuse patterns and anomalous risk scenarios. (Competency: Fraud Risk Identification & Assessment)

Recommendation of Techniques/Tools: Research and recommend advanced techniques and tools for detecting emerging fraud and abuse risks, translating findings into actionable data features for FAMs. (Competency: Risk Assessment)

Claims Analysis: Conduct pre- and post- disbursement claims analysis and in-depth thematic analysis to detect anomalous claims patterns. (Competency: Data Management and Analysis)

Collaboration with SWDA Business Units: Work closely with relevant business units to ensure comprehensive coverage of fraud analytics across end-to-end processes, promoting best practices in fraud detection and risk management. (Competency: Stakeholder Engagement)

","

What we are looking for

  • Proficient in executing job duties with required competencies.
  • Senior Manager: at least 6 years of experience in data analytics, computer/data science, statistics, applied mathematics, business analytics
  • Good analytical skills and conceptual abilities, with a keen eye for identifying key issues and synthesising diverse information into coherent frameworks.
  • Proficiency in quantitative analysis is essential, including the application of statistical techniques and tools such as Tableau, Python, SQL, and VBA to uncover insights and trends, and the ability to communicate these findings in clear, accessible terms.
  • Demonstrates good writing, communication, stakeholder engagement, and project management skills.

Note: This is an individual contributor role.

Successful candidates will be offered a 2-year contract in the first instance and may be considered for an extension or be placed on a permanent tenure

Candidates are encouraged to sign up for a Careers & Skills Passport (CSP) account and include your CSP public profile in your resume. Please check out www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg for details on the CSP.

At the Founders’ Memorial, we are creating a brand-new garden-museum experience for Singaporeans, by Singaporeans. A national landmark at the heart of our garden city, uncovering the story of how independent Singapore came to be, and bringing Singaporeans together to reflect on the heritage of our founding leaders and generation – what it means for us today and for the future. A home for Singapore’s founding values to live on and find new life in its people.

Can you identify with the values that guided our founding leaders and generation that have shaped Singapore to what it is today? Are you keen to tell stories about the courage and resilience exhibited by our founding leaders and generation in our nation-building years (1950s to 1970s)? Do you often think about the challenges and trade-offs that our country must negotiate in the past, present and future? If your answer is ""yes"", join us at the Founders' Memorial!

The FM is seeking a suitable candidate to join the Curatorial team, where you will be part of a passionate team that will help ground the FM’s content and storytelling in solid research and stakeholder engagement. You will be responsible for researching, shaping the content and telling the stories, that will feature in FM’s permanent and temporary galleries as well as for other curatorial projects such as publications, catalogues and digital platforms. You will also work collaboratively with other teams in the FM such as its Education, Interpretation and Digital teams on shaping content for diverse audiences.

","

  • Research and artefact acquisition: Conduct research on primary and secondary material pertaining to Singapore’s post-independence history, including but not limited to oral history interviews and archival records. This includes acquiring artefacts for the National Collection.

  • Knowledge production and new research: Produce knowledge and new research pieces on Singapore's immediate pre- and post-independence history, including but not limited to for use in FM's exhibition galleries and publications. In doing so, you will contribute to FM's thought leadership on Singapore’s immediate pre- and post-independence history.

  • Editorial: Support editorial work for FM's curatorial content in areas such as exhibition text, publications, audio guides and content for digital platforms. This includes ensuring consistency, clarity and accessibility of texts in FM’s institutional voice, and the verification of historical information to ensure accuracy of content.

  • Collaborative curatorial projects: Work collaboratively and coordinate with internal teams within FM in the areas of education, interpretation, digital, programmes as well as other stakeholders such as collection managers, designers, creatives, and translators on the planning and execution of curatorial projects such as publications and audio guides.

","

  • Background in History or the Humanities or other disciplines relevant to Singapore’s post-independence history and nation building policies.

  • Preferably at least 5 years of experience in related curatorial, research and/or editorial work with keen knowledge and passion for Singapore’s post-independence history and heritage, and its relevance to the present and future.

  • Research, Publication & Scholarship - Proven excellence in research and knowledge production, with strong analytical, writing, editorial and presentation skills.

  • Stakeholder Engagement - A collaborative team player with excellent project and stakeholder management skills, and able to work independently.

  • Resourcefulness, and strength in knowledge production, research, project and stakeholder management.

  • As the FM is an institution being built from the ground-up, the candidate should be able to navigate changes, multiple stakeholders and a fast-moving environment, and have adept problem-solving skills where processes are still being established.

Do you love Singapore for punching above its weight as a Little Red Dot? Can you identify with the grit exhibited by our founding leaders and generation as they worked hard to build Singapore to what it is today? Are you keen to explore ideas, leveraging technology to support storytelling and enhance the visitor experience of a Singapore museum? If the answer is ""yes"", join us at the Founders' Memorial (FM)!

At the FM, we are creating a brand-new garden-museum experience for Singaporeans, by Singaporeans. A national landmark at the heart of our garden city, uncovering the story of how independent Singapore came to be, and bringing Singaporeans across generations together to reflect and have bold conversations about what our founding values mean today and for our future.

The FM is seeking a suitable candidate to join the Digital team to develop interactive digital experiences and content for the Founders’ Memorial, across our exhibitions and website, leveraging the potential of digital technology to create compelling, accessible and engaging experiences for our diverse audiences. You will work collaboratively with the Curatorial and Exhibitions teams, and with creatives to present the story of how Singapore came to be, through multi-sensory, emotive and immersive experiences! With the Visitor Experience and Marketing and Communications team, you will leverage digital channels and devices to support a seamless, end-to-end visitor journey of the Founders’ Memorial. Look forward to being a part of creating a living Memorial that unites, challenges and inspires Singaporeans of all generations towards a brighter future!

","

Digital experience development: You will support the development of digital experience for the permanent exhibition, while managing the development and setup of the experience for special exhibitions, contributing to an integrated indoor-outdoor experience of the Memorial. This includes two key areas:

  • Pre- and post- visit experience of the Founders’ Memorial: You will work across teams – including Visitor Experience, Marketing and Communication and Information and Technology – to plan and implement a seamless visitor journey across various digital channels and devices such as social media, online ticketing platforms and digital wayfinding. You will also work with these teams to conduct evaluations and father audience insights into the visitor experience to inform ongoing improvements.

  • Digital brief development: You will collaborate with the Curatorial and Education teams to develop the digital experience brief – comprising technical requirements, desired user experience and suitable digital interventions – for special exhibitions and supporting the development of the digital interactives for the permanent exhibition.

Project management: You will manage the development and setup of digital experience for special exhibitions, including budgeting, managing the procurement, user testing and coordinating with the relevant NHB departments to organise the security testing to ensure that the digital system is robust. Additionally, you will also need to work closely with the Curatorial and Exhibitions teams to develop the feedback mechanism / data collection to track visitors’ responses to the exhibition content and experience, liaising with the appointed vendor and analysing the data collected.

Data management: You will work as a team to tag, organise and store citizens’ stories that are collected through the “Project Citizens” public call, for eventual display at the FM. “Project Citizens” was a campaign launched by the FM in 2025. Since 2025, the Memorial has been collecting stories of the founding generation of citizens through a senior engagement programme which is part of “Project Citizens”. These stories are currently being processed by the Education and Digital officers at the Memorial. You will be part of this project team to process the stories to be presented in the permanent exhibition, while working on the content management system and data management of the stories.

  • Preferably 3-5 years in digital strategy and implementation, preferably in the areas of exhibitions, programmes and visitor experience. An interest or appreciation of Singapore’s history is an advantage.

  • Digital Design & Management - Demonstrated experience in digital media design – including content strategy, art direction, UX/ UI design, wireframing – and developing digital experiences in exhibitions. Basic knowledge of web and frontend technologies, familiarity with the use of platforms such as Matterport 3D and immersive technologies such as AR/VR/MR tools is advantageous.

  • Good project management, analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • A collaborative team player with excellent interpersonal and stakeholder management skills, and able to work well independently.

  • As the FM is an institution being built from the ground-up, the candidate should be able to navigate changes, multiple stakeholders and a fast-moving environment where processes are still being established.

  • Familiarity with or willingness to learn government tools and procurement guidelines will also be essential.

  • Some weekend and after-work hours engagements might be required – candidates should be prepared to exercise some flexibility in the work schedule.

The FM is seeking a suitable candidate to join the Exhibitions team as an experience designer to develop the “FM by Night” experience and special exhibitions. The FM by Night is a special after-hours immersive experience that will transform the Viewing Gallery and outdoor garden of the FM and bring diverse audiences to the FM-Bay East area through light, sound, and multimedia. Our changing special exhibitions will present different themes in Singapore’s pre- and post-independence history in a more accessible and engaging manner to the public.

You will be part of a multidisciplinary internal Exhibition team comprising designers, project managers and digital experts, working alongside a cross-agency project team to bring to life FM by Night. Look forward to being a part of creating a living Memorial that unites, challenges and inspires Singaporeans of all generations towards a brighter future!

","

Experience Design:

  • FM by Night: You will work closely with the Project Manager for FM by Night, and take charge of the experience design, working with the FM project and creative teams to conceptualise the narrative and develop a multisensorial outdoor night experience that leverages the unique FM location. The experience should attract a broad audience – with a particular focus on youth – to explore garden and indoor Viewing Gallery after sunset. In the long run, you will plan and manage the periodic refreshes of FM by Night to keep the experience current to continue attracting new and repeat visitors to the Memorial.

  • Special exhibitions: As a team, you will collaborate with the Education and Curatorial teams to chart the visitor experience and translate the content into interactive, multisensorial and accessible exhibitions. You will identify different partners, including from various industries, to present the content in refreshing and unexpected ways. You will contribute to the full exhibition development cycle, from concept through to delivery, and may need to conduct research to understand the historical context and identify key moments to develop as part of the experience.

Visitor Journey Design: You will map out the end-to-end visitor journey across indoor and outdoor spaces, identifying key engagement points and emotional arcs to guide the narrative development for FM by Night. This includes coordinating with the FM daytime operations to ensure a smooth transition to the night experience and working with the appointed contractors to integrate the light and sound and site elements into a cohesive experience ahead of FM’s opening in 2028.

Outdoor Programming and Activations: In tandem with FM by Night, you will be part of a team that will plan and execute night activations – including supporting marketing efforts and partnerships with external collaborators – to drive visitorship and build community around FM by Night over a longer-term period.

Demonstrated experience in designing visitor or audience experiences, with a strong understanding of narrative, spatial storytelling and audience engagement. Experience in or familiarity with outdoor programmes or activations is an advantage.

Workforce Planning

Digitalisation
